posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked: In general, more heroes tend to make the game easier.  There are, of course, exceptions to this rule - the main ones being Miss Information and the Dreamer.  The straight up damage racing villains like Plague Rat, and Infinitor tend to get much easier with more heroes - their damage output is increased, but the heros get a boost in total HP and damage, so they have the advantage.

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
I'm with Arcanist Lupus, not because of total HP or total damage ability, but just because more heroes get to do more things. They get to play more cards and use more powers. That gives the player team more oportunities to zap an environment card, destroy a villain ongoing card, set up a redirection ability, and so on. The penalty is (generally) increased damage form the villain, but I think that's a good trade for the heroes in the end.

For similar reasons, I think the Atlantean Font of Power dramatically favors the heroes!

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
The biggest reason why 3 heros is generally easier has a lot to do with how damage numbers scale down while damage mitigation stays consistent. In addition to that, damage mitigation is far more valuable with lower damage numbers than higher ones. For example, the difference between taking 0 or 1 damage is more significant than the difference between taking 6 or 7. Damage reduction of 1 is fairly common, even in random groups of 3 heros. With H-2 being by far and large the average instance of damage Villains generally deal, it's a lot more common to completely nullify damage instead of just mitigating it a little bit.

3 Hero games tend to be much longer on average as well compared to 5 hero games because of the lower damage output on both Hero and Villain side while Health Points stay consistent (which works very much in favor of the heavier setup reliant heros such as Absolute Zero).

Because of all of these things, group composition doesn't suffer nearly as much for having some holes as it does in 5 player games. You can get away with not having Ongoing Destruction against Iron Legacy with Bunker, Sentinels, and Legacy (for example), because the sheer amount of damage mitigation they all bring to the table is far more valuable with less heros. You can play AbZero more consistently against more Villains because games are longer and one board wipe does not hurt as much.

posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked:
But Progeny is more likely to be fought by experienced players than by Omnitron, though, and often with hand-picked teams. The fact that the Dark Watch is four of the top five suggests that there's a similar phenomenon at work there, and as for Megalopolis... well, I can't really explain that one, but cherry-picking individual anomalies as an excuse to discount a large bank of data is questionable practice.

In any case, looking at the underlying statistics from the Statistics Project, 'number of heroes' is likely a factor that is primarily determined by number of players, so villain victories by number of players should be fairly reliable, and only four villains of twenty-seven* (The Dreamer, Miss Information, The Ennead and Gloom-Spite) have a higher win-rate with three players than with five.  And as for heroes, with the exception of Prime Warden Tempest (who has equal win rate with 3 and 5 heroes), every hero has a higher win rate with 5. All of them.That's... pretty conclusive.
